nodes.description: MED13 is the hinge subunit that physically tethers the four-protein CDK8 kinase module (CKM: MED13, MED12, CDK8, cyclin C) to core Mediator. Structural work shows MED13 adopts an Argonaute-like bi-lobal fold, and that a large intrinsically disordered region within it forms a principal CKM-core interface which directly occludes the RNA polymerase II and MED26 binding sites — making CKM docking a kinase-independent repressor of Mediator-dependent transcription. Division of labour within the module is asymmetric: MED12 activates CDK8 kinase activity, whereas MED13 mediates the association of the module with Mediator. This node is what MED13 dosage and structural integrity actually control, and is the mechanistic layer the previous version of this entry summarised only as "connective role".

nodes.description: CKM docking on core Mediator sterically blocks RNA polymerase II recruitment, and this repression is independent of CDK8 catalytic activity — MED12 and MED13, not kinase activity, are the critical subunits for it. The module is nevertheless not a pure repressor: CDK8 also acts as a context-dependent co-activator across the p53, Wnt/beta-catenin, serum-response, SMAD and thyroid-hormone-receptor programs. Consequently a perturbation of MED13 dosage dysregulates transcription bidirectionally at CKM-gated promoters and enhancers rather than simply de-repressing them, which is why MED13-related disease is a transcriptional dysregulation disorder and not a straightforward loss of repression.

nodes.description: In a subset of affected individuals, MED13/Mediator dysfunction perturbs cardiac gene-expression programs, contributing to mild and variable congenital heart anomalies. Mutations in the Mediator complex, including MED13 and its paralog MED13L, have been linked to both congenital heart defects and cardiovascular diseases. In the adult heart, MED13 (also known as THRAP1/TRAP240) participates in nuclear-receptor signaling that drives the transcription of genes regulating cardiac and systemic energy homeostasis — this adult-cardiac metabolic role is the best-evidenced mechanism in current literature, with the connection to congenital cardiac developmental programs established by clinical observation and corroborated by mouse genetics demonstrating functional redundancy between Med13 and Med13L in cardiac transcription.

evidence.reference_title: De novo mutations in MED13, a component of the Mediator complex, are associated with a novel neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Six affected individuals had mutations that are predicted to truncate the MED13 protein, six had missense mutations, and one had an in-frame-deletion of one amino acid. Out of the seven non-truncating mutations, six clustered in two specific locations of the MED13 protein: an N-terminal and C-terminal region.

evidence.reference_title: A novel frameshift variant in the MED13 gene causing intellectual developmental disorder-61 in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Intellectual developmental disorder type 61 (MRD61) is an extremely rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by variants in the MED13 gene. This gene encodes a subunit of the mediator complex, which is also known as TRAP, SMCC, DRIP or ARC. This complex functions as a transcriptional coactivator and is essential for the expression of almost all genes. To date, only 26 cases of MRD61 have been reported worldwide.

nodes.description: Several pathogenic missense variants cluster at a conserved phosphodegron (Thr326/Pro327) in MED13. This phosphodegron is normally recognized by the SCF-Fbw7 ubiquitin ligase complex, leading to MED13 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Mutations at these residues may impair MED13 protein turnover, potentially resulting in gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects through accumulation of mutant protein.

nodes.description: MED13 and MED13L are mutually exclusive occupants of the same position in the CKM and are partially redundant, so the intact paralog buffers loss of the other in a tissue-dependent way. Combined cardiomyocyte deletion of both is lethal within weeks where either single deletion is tolerated, and in the early mouse embryo Med13l compensates for Med13 loss during oocyte growth but cannot rescue post-implantation development. This buffering is the most plausible explanation for why MED13 haploinsufficiency produces a predominantly neurodevelopmental phenotype with only mild, variable cardiac involvement, and it is the shared axis linking this entry to MED13L syndrome.

nodes.description: A distinct severe presentation combining marked facial dysmorphism with macroglossia, short stature and macrocephaly was reported in a single patient with a de novo MED13 missense variant. Macrocephaly is notable as the opposite direction of head growth from the microcephaly seen in other MED13 cases, indicating the structural brain phenotype is bidirectional rather than uniformly reductive.

Downstream of MED13/Mediator dysfunction, neuronal gene-expression programs are dysregulated during brain development, contributing to intellectual disability, global developmental delay, language impairment, and variable behavioral phenotypes. Mechanistic studies in mice indicate that MED13 is required cell-autonomously for cortical neuron development: knockdown of Med13 in cortical neurons impairs radial migration, contralateral axonal projection, and dendritic complexity, in part through PlxnA4, linking MED13 dysfunction to the neurodevelopmental disorder phenotype.

nodes.description: MED13 has been recovered as a monogenic cause in an unbiased severe developmental-language-disorder cohort, independent of the intellectual-disability ascertainment route through which the gene was originally found. This is ascertainment-independent corroboration that the MED13 phenotype is language-dominant, and it argues that MED13 belongs on sequencing panels for isolated severe DLD, not only for syndromic intellectual disability.

nodes.description: Three of the thirteen patients in the founding cohort showed characteristics of speech apraxia — a motor-programming speech disorder distinct from the general speech delay recorded for the whole cohort. This matters clinically because apraxia responds to motor-speech therapy techniques rather than generic language therapy, so speech-language assessment in MED13 syndrome should screen for it specifically. Across the cohort, speech production was disproportionately impaired relative to language comprehension.

nodes.description: A conserved, non-transcriptional arm characterised in yeast: under oxidative or nutrient stress, Snf1/AMPK together with the cell-wall-integrity MAPK pathway drive degradation of Med13, and a Snx4/Ksp1-dependent selective-autophagy route provides a second, proteasome-independent clearance path. Destroying Med13 releases cyclin C from its Med13-dependent nuclear anchor to relocalise to mitochondria, where it promotes fission and sensitises cells to regulated cell death. If a mammalian counterpart exists in neurons, MED13-haploinsufficient cells would be predicted to sit closer to the cyclin-C release threshold. The same axis is directly demonstrated in human MED13L patient fibroblasts, which is the strongest argument that it is not purely a yeast phenomenon — but it has not been shown for MED13 in human cells.
nodes.id: Stress-induced Med13 degradation and cyclin C release

evidence.snippet: Upon oxidative stress, cyclin C leaves the nucleus and directly activates the guanosine 5'-triphosphatase (GTPase) Drp1, or Dnm1 in yeast, to induce mitochondrial fragmentation.
